newsitem.title: INDIA: India cuts 97/98 export growth to 10-15 pct.
newsitem.headline: India cuts 97/98 export growth to 10-15 pct.

text.p: The Indian government expects merchandise exports to grow by 10 to 15 percent in 1997/98 (April-March), Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah was quoted on Wednesday as saying.
The projected growth is above the 4.01 percent rate recorded in 1996/97 but below an earlier growth forecast for 1997/98 of 20 percent, the Economic Times said.
"It would be reasonable to expect an export growth of around 10 to 15 percent for the year," the newspaper quoted Ramaiah as saying.
Exports rose by 4.01 percent in 1996/97 to $33.11 billion compared with $31.83 billion in the previous year.
The reduction of the target for 1997/98 follows a drop in exports in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, he said.

The Commerce Ministry reported on Friday that exports fell by 0.95 percent to $8.13 billion in the first quarter of 1997/98. Exports in June grew by 2.53 percent to $2.66 billion from $2.59 billion in the same month in 1996.

Ramaiah attributed the drop in export growth in the first quarter of 1997/98 to a delay in parliamentary approval of the 1997/98 federal budget and the appreciation of the rupee against the U.S. dollar.
The commerce and industry ministries are exploring ways to spur exports, Ramaiah said. The Commerce Ministry is also working out an export strategy which would soon be finalised, he added.
Ramaiah said his ministry would look into the possibility of widening the export basket and including more value-added products in it.

On Monday the commerce minister said the recent appreciation of the rupee against the dollar had affected exports "to some extent", but he said he did not favour a depreciation of the Indian currency.
